title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: K is a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers A (so A^* is the unit group, Galois for simplicity). G is a Lubin–Tate formal group over A attached to a uniformizer π, with formal A-module structure (A acts 'via opérateurs'). The page sets up an application of Tate's 1967 theory of p-divisible groups (Hodge–Tate decomposition of T_p ⊗ C) to G.

Step 1, canonical torsor. T_p(G)(K̄) is an invertible (free rank-1) A-module. Gal(K̄/K) acts on it through the Lubin–Tate character χ_π : Gal(K̄/K) → A^*. Its image is all of A^*, and the fixed field is the totally ramified abelian extension K_π = K(G[π^∞]). The bases (generators) of T_p(G) are permuted simply transitively by Gal(K_π/K).

Step 2, intrinsic choice of K_π. Grothendieck reformulates this as a representability statement. Let T_p(G)^* = lim← G(ν)^* be the functor of generators (A-module generators of the torsion levels). It is a pro-étale A^*-torsor over K, and K_π (as a pro-étale K-algebra) represents it. So there is a canonical pair (K_π, e ∈ T_p(G)^*(K_π)), unique up to unique isomorphism and independent of any choice of algebraic closure. Fixing (K_π, e) and choosing K̄ ⊃ K_π gives an A-linear isomorphism A ≅ T_p(G)(K_π), λ ↦ λe.

Step 3, base change to C. With C = completion of K̄, the boxed diagram reads T_p ≅ A, T_p⊗_{Z_p}A ≅ A⊗_{Z_p}A, T_p⊗_{Z_p}C ≅ A⊗_{Z_p}C, over Z_p → A → C. On T_p⊗C there are two A-actions:
- via the operators of G on T_p;
- via the C-module structure, through the embedding A ⊂ C.
There is also the semilinear action of Gal(K̄/K), which commutes with the operator action of A.

Step 4, where this is heading. The page stops here. Assuming K/Q_p Galois, A⊗_{Z_p}C ≅ ∏_{σ: K→C} C splits by embeddings, so T_p⊗C decomposes into eigenlines indexed by σ. Tate's theorem would then give the expected result: the identity-embedding component is C(1) and the other components are C(0), i.e. χ_π is Hodge–Tate with weight 1 at the identity embedding and weight 0 elsewhere. This is a warm-up example for the comparison / 'mysterious functor' problematic in the 'Cristaux' folder.
errors: The transcription writes T_p(G)⊗_A C. For two distinct A-actions to exist (operators vs. scalars), the tensor product must be over Z_p, as the boxed diagram (A⊗_{Z_p}C) shows. Either Grothendieck slipped or the subscript is misread.

Representability of T_p(G)^* by K_π should be understood pro-étale (K_π as an inverse limit of finite étale K-algebras, i.e. the union of the K(G[π^n])). This is implicit but fine. No mathematical error otherwise; the computation itself is not carried out on this page.

ideas.what: Galois action on T_p of a Lubin–Tate group via χ_π, with the Lubin–Tate extension K_π having group A^*
ideas.modern_name: Lubin–Tate character / local class field theory via Lubin–Tate

ideas.what: K_π as the canonical object (independent of K̄) representing the torsor of generators of T_p(G), with a universal generator e
ideas.modern_name: Lubin–Tate tower as A^*-torsor; universal trivialization of the Tate module
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (cf. Katz, Drinfeld level structures, Lubin–Tate tower)

ideas.what: Applying Tate's Hodge–Tate decomposition to T_p(G)⊗_{Z_p}C, splitting via A⊗_{Z_p}C ≅ ∏_σ C
ideas.modern_name: Hodge–Tate weights of Lubin–Tate characters (weight 1 at identity embedding, 0 elsewhere)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tate 1967 (p-divisible groups); Serre, Abelian l-adic representations 1968

deep.surprise_reason: A standard, unfinished warm-up applying Tate's theory to Lubin–Tate groups. The result (Hodge–Tate weights of χ_π) was already in Tate/Serre by 1967–68. Only historically interesting as showing Grothendieck testing examples inside the 'Cristaux' notes. The neighbouring pages are unrelated Bourbaki drafts on whose backs he wrote.
transcription_corrections: 'T_p(G)⊗_A C' should likely read T_p(G)⊗_{Z_p} C (cf. diagram A⊗_{Z_p}C).
'T_p(G)(\bar K)' correct; 'T_p(G)^*(K_π)' with * meaning set of generators.
